title: Understand Inequalities and Their Solutions
objective: I can graph the solutions of an inequality on a number line.
model: number-line graph: a circle on the boundary (open or closed) and a shaded ray toward the solutions

widgets.component: words to inequality (at least 48, no more than 75, more than 25, less than 40)
widgets.root: Identical to the config warm-up and a fair 8-4 review; keys verified (h ≥ 48, p ≤ 75, s > 25, t < 40).

widgets.component: 'Which graph represents x < 5?' answered by choosing from sentences such as 'Open circle at 5, shaded left'
widgets.root: The lesson's idea is drawing a graph, and the studio ships a number-line drawing activity (act:ineq mode graph) that 8-5 never uses. These nine items are a multiple-choice worksheet about a picture that is described in words and never drawn or shown.
widgets.replacement: Replace 2.1-2.4 and 3.3, 5.3 with act:ineq mode graph (L1 for Practice 2.1-2.4 and 3.3, L2 for 5.3): the student taps the boundary on a number line, toggles open or closed, and drags the ray left or right; graded with named misses (open for ≥, ray toward the wrong side, circle at the wrong number). For Challenge 2.4 and 5.5 use act:ineq graph L3 with the story ('at most 6 clownfish', 'at least 10 years old') shown above the line. Keep 3.1 as a reading item but render it as an nline viz (closed circle at 8, ray left) instead of a sentence.

widgets.component: sort inequalities by open or closed circle
widgets.root: Bins verified (x > 4, x < 12, n > 0 open; x ≥ 7, x ≤ 3, n ≥ 15 closed; t > 0.5 open, t ≥ 0.5 closed). Isolates the circle rule, the lesson's key idea.

widgets.component: find the wrong graphing step: open circle for ≥, shading right for 'fewer than', closed for >, 'I need 7 greater than 7'
widgets.root: Error step indices match the faulty lines; the six faults are the lesson's boundary-inclusion and direction misconceptions.

widgets.component: is a value a solution, which list has only solutions, largest or smallest whole number, read a value off a graph
widgets.root: Sampled 6 seeds at L1-L3: keys right (c = 26 is not a solution of c < 26; 40 is the largest whole solution of w < 41). The nline viz items agree with their key (ray from 27 closed right gives 33; open at 11 left gives 8).

widgets.component: tap every value on a number line that is a solution
widgets.root: mkTest places the boundary, one step either side and, at L3, boundary ± 0.1, so 'close is enough' and 'boundary is always in' are both trapped. This is the right manipulable for 'solutions'; it is not a substitute for graphing.

widgets.component: read the graph back to an inequality
widgets.root: Rendered: open circle at 24 with ray right gives t > 24; closed circle at 3 with ray left gives x ≤ 3. Both keys match.

widgets.component: truth table for d < 30, count solutions in a list, least whole solution of n > 6.5, 4.9 is a solution of y < 5
widgets.root: Cells and counts recomputed (0/1/0/1; 3; 7). Item 4.4 traps 'only whole numbers can be solutions'; 5.1 traps the near-miss x ≤ 7.9.

widgets.component: 'Why did the detective use an open circle at 12?'
widgets.root: There is no detective, graph or story on screen; the question asks about a drawing the student cannot see and can only be answered by elimination from the fourth choice.
widgets.replacement: Show the graph: nline viz min 6, max 18, ray from 12 direction left, open true, and ask 'The graph shows p < 12. Why is the circle at 12 open?' with the same four choices.
